content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe early attempts to classify elements
Explain Mendeleev's contribution to the periodic table
Describe how the modern periodic table differs from Mendeleev's
Explain why some elements were rearranged

is one of chemistry's greatest achievements. It took many scientists over a century to develop, with key contributions from Döbereiner, Newlands, and Mendeleev, before arriving at the modern table we use today.
By the early 1800s, about 60 elements were known. Scientists tried to find patterns.
Johann Döbereiner noticed that some elements could be grouped in threes (triads):
The middle element's atomic mass was roughly the average of the other two.
Only worked for a few elements - couldn't classify all known elements.
John Newlands arranged elements by atomic mass and noticed:
Every eighth element had similar properties
Assumed all elements had been discovered (no gaps)
Put unlike elements together (e.g., iron with oxygen)
created the most successful early periodic table.

Mendeleev left a gap below silicon and called the missing element "eka-silicon."
The accuracy of his predictions proved the table was correct!
Te comes before I in Mendeleev's table, despite having higher atomic mass
This put them in groups with similar elements
Ar (40) should come after K (39) by mass, but properties said otherwise
Not understood - explained odd mass positions
discovered that elements should be arranged by
Triads - groups of three similar elements
Left gaps, predicted elements, swapped some
Arranged by atomic number, not mass
Explain why Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table.
Mendeleev arranged elements by properties as well as atomic mass
Sometimes no known element fitted the expected position
He assumed these elements existed but hadn't been discovered
He predicted the properties of the missing elements
When these elements were discovered later, his predictions were accurate
This proved his periodic table was correct
Mendeleev placed tellurium before iodine, even though tellurium has a higher atomic mass. Explain why.
Mendeleev prioritised chemical properties over atomic mass
Tellurium has properties similar to sulfur and selenium (Group 6)
Iodine has properties similar to chlorine and bromine (Group 7)
Placing them in strict mass order would put them in the wrong groups
Mendeleev swapped them so they were with similar elements
This was later justified when atomic number was discovered (Te=52, I=53)
State one advantage and one disadvantage of Mendeleev's table compared to earlier attempts.
Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties, which were later proved correct.
He had to swap some elements (like Te and I) from strict mass order, and couldn't explain why this was necessary until proton number was discovered.
Thinking Mendeleev arranged by atomic number
Mendeleev used atomic MASS; Moseley later used atomic NUMBER
Thinking Newlands' octaves worked for all elements
It only worked up to calcium and was later ridiculed
Thinking the periodic table was created by one person
It was developed over time by many scientists
Triads - middle element's mass = average of other two
Octaves - properties repeat every 8 elements (limited success)

Arranged by atomic number (protons), not mass
